title: Perfect derived sections of a perfect complex on a flat proper space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces and schemes are [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme]. Use the small etale site with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the full subcategory whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect object means an object locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a flat proper finitely presented algebraic space. Flatness is checked on etale charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]; proper means separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type on etale charts and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation on etale charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. For every perfect $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, the unbounded right derived global sections $R\Gamma(X,E)$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], taken as an object of $D(A)$ through $A\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, are perfect: they are isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Spectra are [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Tag 0CTM, lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general (1), over an affine base; affine identification with ring complexes uses lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site.

proof.text: Put $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $G^\bullet=\mathcal O_X[0]$. This is a bounded complex of quasi-coherent finitely presented modules: its only nonzero term has the one-generator presentation $0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_X\to0$. Its geometric stalks are flat over $U$ by flatness of $f$, and its annihilator is zero, so its support as a closed subspace is $X$, proper over $U$. Thus all coefficient-complex hypotheses of the proper-support tensor theorem hold, with $S=Y=U$ and the given finitely presented $f$.

source.place: Tag 0CTM, lemma-flat-proper-perfect-direct-image-general, proof (1): take the structure module in degree zero

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-proper-support-tensor-perfect] with this $G^\bullet$ and the given perfect $E$. It gives a perfect object with quasi-coherent cohomology $K=Rf_*(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_X[0])=Rf_*E$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. The equality uses the tensor unit: on a K-flat representative for $E$, tensoring each term with $\mathcal O_X$ is the identity, including differentials.

Let $L=R\epsilon_{U,*}K$. The quasi-coherent equivalence [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison] puts $L$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{Zar}})$ and gives $\epsilon_U^*L\cong K$. By [lem-sfb-etale-detects-perfect], $L$ is Zariski perfect. Apply [lem-pc-perfect-affine-bounded-projective] to the affine scheme $U$: there is a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules with $L\cong\widetilde{P^\bullet}$.

source.place: Tags 071Q, lemma-derived-quasi-coherent-small-etale-site, and 08HG, lemma-descend-perfect; perfect.tex Tag 08EB, lemma-perfect-affine

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $f:X_{\mathrm{et}}\to U_{\mathrm{et}}$ followed by the global-sections map to the one-point site with ring $A$. Its composite is global sections on $X$ with scalars induced by $f$, so $R\Gamma(X,E)\cong R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{et}},K)$ in $D(A)$. The global-sections comparison of [lem-sfb-scheme-derived-etale-qcoh-comparison] and $\epsilon_U^*L\cong K$ identify the latter with $R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{Zar}},L)$. Finally [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] gives $R\Gamma(U_{\mathrm{Zar}},\widetilde{P^\bullet})\cong P^\bullet$. The composite is an isomorphism in $D(A)$, proving the claimed perfectness.
